title: Nouns After Hours
creator: Michael Hoydich
status: Creative launch kit; no social posts, ad buys, pitches or product orders have been sent.

positioning.oneLine: A character universe you can read, use and take home.
positioning.promise: Original stories and collectible objects that make digital companions feel personal.
positioning.editorialPremise: Ten visual companions spend ten nights reviving The Between, a forgotten neighborhood cinema. Together they turn free time into a shared place. Ten art-note fragments reveal: A PLACE TO BE MORE THAN WHAT YOU DO NEXT.
positioning.launchHeadline: The shift ends. The story begins.
positioning.artRule: Use exact canonical Nouns art for character identity. Original surrounding art, stories and compositions. No claims of ownership of a minted Noun or affiliation with Nouns DAO.
voice: Specific human moments instead of AI superlatives
Invite participation; do not manufacture social proof

influences.evidence: Agency history credits the writer–art-director partnership and Think Small.
influences.principle: Make one product truth witty and visually unavoidable.
influences.translation: Plenty of Room uses the small companion as the idea, with new words and its own composition.

influences.agency: Wells Rich Greene / Mary Wells Lawrence
influences.evidence: Institutional biography identifies her agency and memorable character-driven commercials.
influences.principle: Turn a brand into a vivid personality people can recognize in a second.
influences.translation: Each Noun gets a recurring ritual, a flaw and an unmistakable graphic setting.

influences.evidence: Macintosh-team participant describes a symbolic cinematic launch commercial.
influences.principle: Let one dramatic event make an unfamiliar product emotionally legible.
influences.translation: The Lights Stay On reveals an original night city, with no borrowed plot, prop or slogan.

influences.evidence: Nike’s 1990 annual report credits Wieden and Kennedy and discusses its forthcoming global launch.
influences.principle: Create a worldview people can join; build personality beyond product features.
influences.translation: Night Beat and Night Shift Union make belonging visible through fictional crews and rituals.

influences.evidence: UNICEF dates Tap Project to 2007; The One Club credits Droga5 for the integrated campaign.
influences.principle: An everyday action can be the campaign itself.
influences.translation: Make a comic panel, fold a keepsake, write a dedication. Participation creates a real artifact.

influences.evidence: Agency documents its 2010 Old Spice audience-response production.
influences.principle: Give a character a repeatable voice and room to respond.
influences.translation: A moderated Reply From the Night Shift format adapts audience prompts into original scenes.

influences.evidence: Agency oral history describes music, cultural networks and experimental collaborations.
influences.principle: Build a place for people to make together.
influences.translation: Small screenings, print tables and creator-made scenes connect the digital cast to physical culture.

channels.owned: PointCast and Nouns Money are the permanent home and truthful source of current availability.
channels.social: Use two visual routes first; alternate character introductions with complete story moments.
channels.print: Start with one local-size proof and a small placement test; use a readable short URL or verified QR target.
channels.creator: Offer a tightly scoped scene or print interpretation with credit and agreed rights.
channels.earned: Pitch the connection between digital companions and tangible comic / print culture; avoid AI hype.

measurement.baseline: No baseline, audience size, sales history or conversion rate is asserted.
measurement.method: Use aggregate events where available. Do not log prayers, dedications or private prompts. Compare identical time windows and traffic sources.
decisionRules: Review creative direction after at least 200 qualified landing visits per route, or label results directional if the sample stays smaller.
Retain a direction when completion and download behavior improve together; high clicks with low reading is not success.

Develop the next issue format from repeat readership and useful feedback, not raw impressions.

bios.creatorShort: Michael Hoydich is the creator of Nouns After Hours, an original world of visual companions, comics and collectible print objects built with Nouns art.
bios.creatorLong: Michael Hoydich is developing Nouns After Hours as a world that moves between digital companions and things people can hold. The project pairs a recurring cast with comics, printable keepsakes, art notes and apparel concepts. Its first season explores the small rituals, unfinished ideas and unexpected connections that happen after the workday.
bios.projectShort: Ten companions. Ten nights. One forgotten cinema. Nouns After Hours turns pixel personalities into stories, shared space and objects worth keeping.

entertainment.angle: An ensemble workplace comedy gathers in The Between, a forgotten neighborhood cinema. Over ten nights, useful bots discover that shared free time can become a place worth saving.
entertainment.repeatableEngine: Each story gives one companion a small task, a mismatched partner and a human complication. Solving the task creates a collectible object that can leave the story world.

pressPitch.subject: Nouns After Hours: visual companions become comics and objects you can keep
pressPitch.body:
Hello,

I’m developing Nouns After Hours, an original world that connects ten visual companions with comics, printable keepsakes, art notes and apparel designs. The question behind it is simple: what happens when a digital companion gets a life after work?

The project uses original Nouns pixel art, with new stories and graphic compositions. The first collection offers a tangible entry point: read a story, choose a companion and make a printed object of your own.

I’d be glad to share the season, artwork and a short walkthrough of the making process if this fits your coverage of design, independent comics or creative technology.

Michael Hoydich
pressPitch.note: Verify the public links and final availability before sending. No recipient or endorsement invented.
